summary.headline: The Select Board declined to back a $100,000 debt retention for Breakneck Hill and tabled a town procurement policy.
summary.summary: The Select Board heard an update on an ongoing town government structure study from consultant Bill Keegan ahead of a planned public forum and December report. The board reviewed preparations and article assignments for the upcoming October 17 Special Town Meeting, voting unanimously against sponsoring a floor amendment to retain $100,000 in unissued borrowing for Breakneck Hill restoration. Members also tabled an administration-drafted procurement conflict-of-interest policy, deeming it duplicative of state ethics law and overly burdensome for small town vendors.

topics.title: Town government structure study update
topics.summary: Consultant Bill Keegan of Capital Strategic Solutions briefed the board on the comprehensive government structure study commissioned by the town. Keegan reported strong survey participation across boards and department heads, and outlined plans for individual interviews and an early November public forum before presenting final recommendations in December.
key_details: Keegan noted that 87% of Massachusetts municipalities have professional administrators, including 68 town managers and 179 town administrators.
Survey results from town staff, committees, and elected officials showed strong engagement and identified operational strengths and improvement areas.
A public listening session with a remote participation option is planned for early November.
Keegan plans to conduct one-on-one interviews with Select Board members and department heads.
A final report containing a phased implementation plan is scheduled for delivery in December.
topics.outcome: Select Board members agreed to schedule individual interviews with Keegan, and staff will coordinate dates for the November public listening session.

topics.title: Board and administration updates and grant awards
topics.summary: Board members and the town administrator provided operational updates, announced several state and federal grant awards, and introduced the interim town clerk. Major announcements included state approval of an additional liquor license for Costco, more than $1.3 million in competitive grants, and early voting logistics for the November election.
key_details: The governor signed a special act authorizing an additional off-premises alcohol license for Costco, with the town having until October 4, 2023 to issue it.

Grants announced: $1.1 million MassWorks grant for Southville Road water main replacement (1,300 feet of pipe), $150,000 for Route 9/I-495 corridor study with Westborough, $86,857.14 FEMA grant for fire hoses, and $20,559 traffic safety grant.
Amy Berry was sworn in as interim town clerk following Jim Hegarty's retirement; in-person early voting runs October 17–30 with 1,793 mail-in ballots already mailed.
Heritage Park added outdoor game amenities funded by a Choate Fund grant; the combination code for the game box is 1727 (the town's incorporation year).
The Neary Elementary School Building Committee reported five renovation and repair options ranging from $33 million to $49 million, plus a requested lower-cost $15 million scope.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved consent agenda items, amended prior meeting minutes, and approved a public works contract for facility door replacements.
key_details: Approved meeting minutes of September 24, 2020.
Approved amended meeting minutes of September 15, 2020 correcting minor typographical errors.
Approved an overhead door replacement contract with Door Systems for $161,545, well below the $287,500 authorized amount.

topics.title: Article 6: Breakneck Hill debt authorization rescission
topics.summary: The board considered a request from the Stewardship Committee and Conservation Commission to amend Article 6 on the Special Town Meeting floor. Instead of rescinding the full $727,960 in remaining unissued borrowing for the Breakneck Hill remediation project, the committees sought to retain $100,000 to fund ecological habitat restoration and contractor repair work.
key_details: Town Meeting previously authorized $4.327 million for Breakneck Hill dump cleanup, borrowing $3.6 million to date.
Approximately $176,000 in previously borrowed funds remains available for ongoing restoration.
Stewardship Committee Chair Joyce Greenleaf requested retaining $100,000 in unissued borrowing to address heavy equipment damage, soil compaction, wetland gravel removal, and meadow replanting.
The remediation contractor credited $45,000 back to the town for work not completed, which is part of the remaining $176,000 balance.
Select Board members opposed retaining the borrowing, citing tight town finances, lack of detailed cost estimates, and existing unspent borrowed balances.
topics.outcome: The board voted 5-0 against sponsoring or supporting a floor amendment to reduce the debt rescission by $100,000.
topics.why_it_matters: Rescinding the full $727,960 in authorized borrowing closes out long-standing project debt capacity and prevents the town from issuing additional debt for site restoration without future Town Meeting approval.

topics.title: Special Town Meeting warrant review and article assignments
topics.summary: The board finalized the logistics and assigned board members to present motions for the eight articles on the October 17, 2020 Special Town Meeting warrant. Members discussed projected article flow and debate expectations.
key_details: Special Town Meeting scheduled for October 17, 2020 at 10:00 a.m. at Trottier Middle School.
Article 1 (appointed town clerk): Chair to move, deferred to Jim Hegarty.
Article 2 (downtown zoning amendment): Tim Bricket to move, deferred to Zoning Board of Appeals.
Article 6 (rescinding debt): Sam Stivers to move.
Article 7 (water main extension for 2 properties near landfill): Andrew Dennington to move.
Article 8 (assessor parcel mapping): Sam Stivers assigned as backup if Board of Assessors chair does not move.
topics.outcome: Motions assigned among board members; no formal vote required.

topics.title: Draft procurement and conflict of interest policy
topics.summary: The board reviewed a proposed municipal procurement conflict-of-interest policy drafted to fulfill state best practice recommendations. Board members criticized the draft as largely copying state conflict-of-interest statutes while introducing unrealistic requirements, such as mandating audited financial statements for prequalified contractors.
key_details: The draft policy was developed following Division of Local Services recommendations.
Members noted that state law (M.G.L. c. 268A) and state ethics training already govern public employee procurement conflicts.
Section requiring audited financial statements from contractors was flagged as prohibitive for local small-scale contractors.
Board members expressed concern over redundant policies creating administrative confusion without adding legal force.
topics.outcome: The board voted to table the policy indefinitely.

votes.motion: Approve consent agenda items B through L and N, and the minutes of September 24, 2020.
Approve the minutes of September 15, 2020, as amended.
Approve consent agenda item M, the contract with Door Systems for overhead door replacements in the amount of $161,545.
Support or sponsor an amendment on the Town Meeting floor to reduce the Article 6 debt rescission amount from $727,960 to $627,960.
Table the procurement conflict of interest policy indefinitely.
Enter into executive session under M.G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(3) to discuss contract negotiations for the Fire Chief, not to return to open session.

public_comment.summary: Stewardship Committee Chair Joyce Greenleaf requested that the board not rescind $100,000 of authorized debt for Breakneck Hill under Article 6, arguing the funds are necessary to restore native plant diversity and repair soil compaction and wetland damage caused by remediation equipment.
